items.title: Election Day underway; Trump sows doubt on results
items.feedTitle: Election Day underway after a surge in early voting, as Trump sows doubt on results
items.summary: Americans are voting in midterm elections that will determine control of Congress, with Trump spending months attempting to influence outcomes and casting doubt on electoral integrity before polls closed. The elections represent a significant test of his political strength and the stability of democratic institutions. Results will begin arriving at 6 p.m. ET in Kentucky and Indiana, with major variables affecting the final outcomes.

items.title: Florida experiences half year's rainfall in 36 hours
items.feedTitle: Parts of Florida see half a year’s worth of rain in 36 hours
items.summary: Parts of Florida received historic rainfall amounts in a single 36-hour period, with some areas getting the equivalent of six months' worth of precipitation. The flooding created significant disruptions and cleanup efforts across affected regions. Residents faced rising floodwaters and widespread property damage from the extreme weather event.

items.title: Trump says US will end $4 billion military aid to Israel
items.feedTitle: As Americans vote, Trump says US will stop $4 billion in aid to Israel
items.summary: On Election Day, Trump announced the US would terminate the $4 billion annual military aid package to Israel by year-end, a surprise statement that appeared targeted at voters skeptical of US support for the country. The announcement came during voting and sparked immediate market and diplomatic reactions. Oil prices tumbled on the news, suggesting markets interpreted it as potentially reducing regional tensions.

items.title: New York measles death first in over 30 years
items.feedTitle: New York reports first measles-associated death in more than 30 years
items.summary: A child in upstate New York's Lewis County died from measles, marking the state's first measles-related death in more than 30 years. State and local health officials are investigating the case and its public health implications. The death highlights concerns about measles transmission in areas with lower vaccination rates.

items.title: West Point cadet drugged girlfriend to force abortion
items.feedTitle: A West Point cadet drugged his girlfriend to force an unwanted abortion. Then he graduated from Cornell
items.summary: A former West Point cadet is facing legal action after allegedly drugging his girlfriend and forcing abortion pills into her body without consent. He subsequently graduated from Cornell University, raising questions about institutional accountability and oversight. The case involves serious criminal allegations related to reproductive coercion and bodily autonomy violations.

stlouis.title: DOJ monitors St. Louis polls for election violations
stlouis.feedTitle: Justice Department to monitor polls in St. Louis, Metro East for election violations
stlouis.summary: The Department of Justice is monitoring polling places in St. Louis and the Metro East (St. Clair and Madison Counties) on Election Day to watch for potential violations. This federal oversight occurs amid national concerns about election integrity and voting access. The monitoring reflects ongoing attention to ensuring fair voting practices in key regions.

stlouis.title: 22,000 Missouri immigrants projected to lose status by 2028
stlouis.feedTitle: Policy advocates: 22,000 immigrants in Missouri projected to lose status by 2028
stlouis.summary: Policy advocates warn that approximately 22,000 immigrants in Missouri are projected to lose their legal status by 2028 under current policies and enforcement trends. The projection reflects concerns about the impact of immigration restrictions on vulnerable populations in the state. Advocates are calling for policy changes to address the anticipated loss of status.

stlouis.title: HindiUSA St. Louis grows Hindi student enrollment tenfold
stlouis.feedTitle: HindiUSA St. Louis Grows From 22 to 240 Hindi Students
stlouis.summary: Hindi language programs in St. Louis have experienced dramatic growth, with student enrollment increasing from 22 to 240 students. The expansion reflects growing interest in Hindi language and culture in the St. Louis area. The program's success indicates strong community demand for Indian language education.

items.title: Russian strikes kill 31 at Ukrainian aid center; dozens missing
items.feedTitle: Death toll hits 31 after Russian strikes on a Ukrainian aid site, with dozens still missing
items.summary: Russian forces dropped at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs on a humanitarian aid center in Komyshuvakha village in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 31 people and leaving more than 45 residents missing. Emergency workers searched through debris and rubble, pulling bodies from the cratered blast site. The attack is among the deadliest strikes on civilian targets during the war.

items.title: US launches defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
items.feedTitle: US strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island as Vance voices optimism about a deal
items.summary: The US launched limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Monday, reportedly targeting surface-to-air missiles. US officials characterized the strikes as defensive and in response to Iranian attacks on US assets. The strikes occurred on the eve of US midterm elections amid ongoing tensions and diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict.

items.title: Seven European flights hit by false bomb threats
items.feedTitle: Bomb threats on flights cause disruption in Europe, no devices found
items.summary: Seven planes across Europe were searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats on Tuesday, affecting flights in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria, Italy, and the UK. The threats were determined to be false alarms and no explosives were found. The incidents included two UK departures and several Ryanair services, causing significant disruption to air traffic.

items.title: Nordic nations refuse to face Russia in ice hockey World Championship
items.feedTitle: Nordic nations refuse to face Russia in ice hockey World Championship
items.summary: Summary unavailable for this update.

items.title: King Charles acknowledges Britain's 'shameful' role in slave trade
items.feedTitle: King tells Commonwealth leaders that Britain’s role in slave trade was ‘shameful’ but stops short of apology – as it happened
items.summary: King Charles told Commonwealth leaders that Britain's role in the slave trade was 'shameful' during his opening address at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua. However, he stopped short of issuing a formal apology for slavery and its legacy. The speech marks formal opening of discussions on historical accountability and reparations among Commonwealth nations.

items.title: India-China border tensions escalate in Arunachal Pradesh
items.feedTitle: What's behind new India-China border tensions in Arunachal Pradesh state?
items.summary: Fresh tensions have emerged along the India-China border in Arunachal Pradesh state, highlighting ongoing territorial disputes between the two nations. The incidents reflect persistent military and political friction along the contested frontier. The tensions underscore the fragility of border management between the two regional powers.

items.title: Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu wins India's first Youth Olympics wushu medal
items.feedTitle: Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu makes history, wins India's first Youth Olympics wushu medal
items.summary: Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu made history by winning India's first-ever Youth Olympics medal in wushu at the Games. The achievement represents a breakthrough for the martial art in Indian international competition. Her victory highlights growing Indian participation and success in non-traditional Olympic sports.

items.title: Welfare payments to use voter ID instead of Aadhaar
items.feedTitle: Welfare payments will be based on voter IDs, not Aadhaar, says Panchayati Raj Minister
items.summary: India's Panchayati Raj Minister announced that welfare payments will be based on voter IDs (EPIC numbers) with biometrics rather than Aadhaar as currently practiced. The policy shift aims to change how welfare benefits are distributed and verified. The move reflects ongoing debates about identity documentation and welfare access in India.

items.title: India pulled 500 million people out of poverty, inequality deepens
items.feedTitle: How India pulled 500 million people out of poverty as inequality deepens
items.summary: India has achieved remarkable progress in reducing poverty, lifting approximately 500 million people out of poverty over recent decades according to World Bank assessment. However, this progress masks deepening inequality within the country. The data highlights India's economic growth achievements while revealing persistent disparities in wealth distribution.

items.title: Indian seafarer killed in ship attack near Oman
items.feedTitle: Indian seafarer killed in attack on ship in West Asia; toll rises to 23
items.summary: An Indian seafarer was killed in an attack on a ship in West Asia near Oman, with 13 others rescued from the vessel. The incident marks the 23rd reported fatality from maritime attacks in the region. India's Ministry of External Affairs called for de-escalation as attacks on commercial shipping continue in contested waters.

immigration.title: USCIS cuts work permit validity from 5 to 18 months
immigration.feedTitle: USCIS Rule: Work permit validity cut from 5 years to 18 months for millions of immigrants with pending cases
immigration.summary: USCIS implemented a rule change reducing employment authorization document (EAD) validity from 5 years to 18 months for millions of immigrants with pending cases. The rule is now permanent and finalized, affecting workers awaiting green card processing. This restriction significantly increases renewal frequency and associated costs for affected immigrants.

immigration.title: Court blocks reopening of 2027 Green Card Lottery
immigration.feedTitle: US court blocks order to reopen 2027 Green Card Lottery
immigration.summary: A federal appeals court upheld a freeze on reopening the FY 2027 Diversity Visa Lottery program, blocking efforts to reopen applications. The ruling allows the Trump administration's suspension of the visa lottery to continue despite Congressional mandate for the program. The decision leaves the 2027 lottery closed and applicants unable to participate.

immigration.title: Federal Register: automatic work permit extensions ended
immigration.feedTitle: Removal of Automatic Extensions for Certain Employment Authorization Documents
immigration.summary: USCIS published a rule on October 30, 2025, that ended automatic extensions of employment authorization documents (Forms I-766/EAD) for workers who timely filed renewal applications. The rule is finalized and in effect, requiring workers to secure new authorization before expiration rather than relying on automatic 540-day extensions. The change significantly impacts workers with pending applications.

items.title: Oil prices fall on Iran deal hopes amid US strikes
items.feedTitle: Oil price falls amid hope of a breakthrough to end Iran war
items.summary: Brent crude oil fell to $105.55 per barrel, its lowest level in more than two weeks, as markets grew hopeful for a diplomatic breakthrough to end the Iran conflict. The decline of more than 6.5% reflects investor optimism despite ongoing US military strikes on Iranian targets. Oil prices remain volatile amid geopolitical tensions.

items.title: India's Sensex surges 1,225 points; Nifty at two-month high
items.feedTitle: Sensex Jumps 1,225 Points as Strong Corporate Earnings Fuel Rally in Indian Stocks
items.summary: The BSE Sensex jumped 1,225 points as Indian markets extended a four-day rally, driven by strong corporate earnings, foreign investor buying, and falling crude oil prices. The Nifty 50 crossed 23,800 for the first time since August, hitting a two-month high. The rally reflects improved sentiment on macro pressures easing and healthy corporate performance.

items.title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq edge higher ahead of midterms
items.feedTitle: S&P 500, Nasdaq rise as tech stocks gain ahead of midterm results
items.summary: US stock markets opened mixed on Election Day with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq edging higher despite Apple's decline following earnings disappointment. Oil price declines and tech stock strength offset losses in other sectors. Markets remain cautious ahead of midterm election results that could determine control of Congress.

items.title: Binance hackers used fake job interviews in $6.3 billion attack
items.feedTitle: Binance hackers used fake job interview in $6.3 billion attack
items.summary: Binance revealed that hackers orchestrated the record-breaking $6.3 billion crypto theft by using fake job interview invitations to target company engineers. The attackers impersonated legitimate recruiters and conducted bogus interviews with fake Binance representatives. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng says customers will not lose funds as the exchange covers losses.

items.title: Saudi Aramco profit surges despite pipeline attacks
items.feedTitle: Saudi Aramco Profit Jumps Despite Damaging Attacks on Pipelines and Refineries
items.summary: Saudi Aramco's third-quarter profits jumped by approximately one-third despite damage to pipelines and refineries from attacks on oil infrastructure. Higher oil prices offset production disruptions from the attacks. The earnings highlight the company's resilience and the impact of geopolitical tensions on energy markets.

finance.note: Oil prices tumbled over 6% to $105.55/barrel as markets grew hopeful for a US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough, offsetting supply concerns from US strikes on Iranian targets. US equities opened mixed on Election Day with S&P 500 and Nasdaq edging higher despite Apple's earnings disappointment; India's Sensex surged 1,225 points on strong earnings and foreign buying. Watch: midterm election outcomes determining Congressional control, potential market reaction to Democratic gains/Republican losses, and further developments in Iran negotiations affecting energy markets.

cards.title: Sleep and cognitive resilience
cards.insight: Quality sleep is foundational to mental resilience and emotional regulation. When sleep is disrupted—whether by stress, illness, or external pressure—cognitive function, decision-making, and stress tolerance all decline. Sleep deprivation compounds the impact of anxiety and makes it harder to process and recover from daily challenges.
cards.takeaway: Protect sleep as a non-negotiable health priority; aim for 7–9 hours nightly and maintain consistent sleep/wake times to strengthen your mental fortitude.

cards.title: Movement as mood regulation
cards.insight: Physical activity directly influences brain chemistry, boosting serotonin, dopamine, and endorphins—all critical for mood stability. Even moderate movement (a 15–20 minute walk) can interrupt rumination and provide immediate relief from anxiety or low mood. Consistency matters more than intensity.
cards.takeaway: Integrate brief movement breaks into your day, especially during stressful periods, to naturally regulate mood without relying solely on other interventions.

cards.title: Nutrition and mental clarity
cards.insight: The gut-brain connection is bidirectional: what you eat affects neurotransmitter production, inflammation levels, and cognitive performance. Diets high in ultra-processed foods correlate with higher rates of depression and anxiety, while whole foods support stable mood and focus. Blood sugar stability is particularly important for sustained mental energy.
cards.takeaway: Prioritize whole foods, stable blood sugar through balanced meals, and adequate protein and omega-3s to support mental clarity and emotional resilience.

cards.title: Social connection and loneliness resilience
cards.insight: Loneliness is a measurable physiological stressor that accelerates aging and increases disease risk. Conversely, meaningful social connection—even brief, authentic interactions—buffers against stress, reduces inflammation markers, and improves both mental and physical health. Quality matters far more than quantity of relationships.
cards.takeaway: Invest intentionally in one or two deep relationships and regular, unrushed time with people who understand you; isolation is both preventable and reversible.

ai.title: Anthropic grapples with worsening compute margins despite scale
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute
ai.summary: Despite scaling its operations, Anthropic is facing deteriorating compute margins—a concerning sign given that economics should improve with larger scale. The company's financial efficiency in running AI models is declining, raising questions about its path to profitability ahead of its IPO. This suggests fundamental challenges in the cost structure of large language model operations.

ai.title: Anthropic warns AI capable of improving itself soon
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic warns that it’s very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI
ai.summary: Anthropic has issued a warning in its SEC filings that AI models may soon reach the capability of recursive self-improvement (RSI)—the point at which AI becomes skilled enough to train and improve itself without human intervention. This milestone, if reached, could trigger dramatic acceleration in AI capabilities that may exceed human control. The warning reflects the company's assessment of near-term AI development trajectories.

ai.title: Google restricts Search access for schools banning AI
ai.feedTitle: Google will let schools disable its AI tools, but not without sacrificing Search
ai.summary: Google announced that schools choosing to restrict or ban its AI tools entirely will lose access to Google Search, as AI features are now deeply integrated into the search engine. The policy effectively forces schools to accept AI integration or forfeit access to core Google services. The move has raised concerns about digital equity and student choice in education.

ai.title: New York Times sues Brave browser over content scraping
ai.feedTitle: New York Times and other outlets sue web browser Brave over alleged content scraping
ai.summary: The New York Times and other media outlets sued privacy-focused web browser Brave for allegedly scraping copyrighted content and distributing it to customers without authorization, including AI companies like Anthropic and Perplexity. The lawsuit alleges unlawful content distribution to third parties. The case highlights ongoing copyright tensions between media companies and AI firms.

ai.title: 42AI launches with $62.5M; claims AI can predict human behavior
ai.feedTitle: 42AI comes out of stealth with $62.5M and a world model that can ‘predict human behavior’
ai.summary: Startup 42AI emerged from stealth mode with $62.5 million in funding and claims to have developed a world model capable of predicting human behavior in entirely new situations. The company's technology raises significant ethical and practical questions about behavioral prediction and its applications. The funding reflects investor interest in next-generation AI capabilities.
